correction_notice: Round 13: historical round-12 records below are preserved, not current advice. The superseding correction replaces B2 interpretation/limit, decision_procedure step 2, SC1/SC2 fixture attribution and the corresponding MD current-host/R13 claims. ProtectSystem=no plus empty ReadOnlyPaths does not exclude another unit-side read-only path view.
scope: Read-only diagnostic classification of ordinary mkdir/mkdirat create-class failures at a target path (EACCES / EROFS / EEXIST families) for the rollback-net surface. Branch records are API-grounded distinctions and controls, not four simultaneously live host causes; host causal attribution is explicitly unproven. This matrix classifies mkdir-class outcomes; it is not proof of the Btrfs subvolume ioctl path or of any historical host cause.
independence: C2 is independent of the C1 census arm: no census script, census output, census fixture or root-metadata census field is read or required by this matrix.

evidence.quote: The parent directory does not allow write permission to the process, or one of the directories in path did not allow search permission.
Bypass file read, write, and execute permission checks.
Adjust the access mode, user and group ownership, and restore the SELinux security context of a file or directory, if it exists.

branches.interpretation: Creating an entry requires write (and search) permission on the parent; a parent mode/ACL that denies write to the caller's identity fails the create with EACCES. The same EACCES sentence also covers the search variant: a path-prefix directory without search permission fails EACCES even when the immediate parent is writable. DAC denial alone produces EACCES only when the caller has no bypass capability (conjunction with B3).

discriminator.expected_signal: mode/ACL grants no write to the caller on the parent, or no search (x) on a path-prefix directory — e.g. 0555 root:root with base-only ACL entries

branches.limit: DAC denial is necessary but not sufficient to attribute an observed EACCES: with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE the same mode succeeds (S027). Mode 0555 is a DAC bit pattern on an inode, not a mount property; on a rw mount it yields EACCES, never EROFS. On this host the 0555 root mode is a vendor-configured systemd tmpfiles rule (S040: /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf line 10, `z / 555 - - -`, owned by systemd 261.2-1; S039 for the `z` mode semantics), so it is not evidence of corruption and this matrix does not recommend changing it. Whether the mode is healthy policy belongs to the C1 root-metadata finding, not this branch.

evidence.quote: path refers to a file on a read-only filesystem.
If true, mounts the /usr/ and the boot loader directories (/boot and /efi) read-only for processes invoked by this unit.
If set to "full", the /etc/ directory is mounted read-only, too.
If set to "strict" the entire file system hierarchy is mounted read-only, except for the API file system subtrees /dev/, /proc/ and /sys/
Note that ReadWritePaths= cannot be used to gain write access to a file system whose superblock is mounted read-only.

branches.interpretation: ProtectSystem=full covers /usr/, /boot/, /efi/ and /etc/ only; it does not cover /. ProtectSystem=strict mounts the entire hierarchy read-only except the API subtrees, and a ReadOnlyPaths= entry can cover a specific target. A read-only superblock, a covering ReadOnlyPaths= entry, or ProtectSystem=strict fails create-class writes with EROFS, independent of DAC mode and of capabilities. EROFS is a different errno from EACCES, so an observed EACCES is not explained by this branch. On this host the unit has ProtectSystem=no and empty ReadOnlyPaths=, so B2 is not configured for /.

commands: systemctl show -p ProtectSystem -p ReadOnlyPaths -p ReadWritePaths -p BindReadOnlyPaths -p TemporaryFileSystem -p RootDirectory -p RootImage <unit>
discriminator.expected_signal: ro in the target mount's VFS or FS options, or ProtectSystem=strict, or a ReadOnlyPaths=/BindReadOnlyPaths= entry covering the target, or TemporaryFileSystem= mounting over it — ProtectSystem=full alone does not cover /; RootDirectory=/RootImage= change the unit's path view

branches.evidence_kind: current host mount namespace + configured unit text; unit-private namespace unobserved
branches.limit: findmnt reads the host mount namespace, not the unit's private namespace, so a unit-private read-only bind or temporary superblock remount is invisible to a later global read; a host findmnt can never exclude a unit-private namespace or another sandbox mechanism. The unit-side signal is the manager's configured property text; BindReadOnlyPaths=, TemporaryFileSystem=, RootDirectory= and RootImage= can also change the unit's view, but they were not part of the captured property set in this round. ProtectSystem=full does not cover / (S028), so only strict or a ReadOnlyPaths= entry can make / read-only through the unit. No read-only filesystem was mounted and no EROFS write attempt was performed in this round's fixtures, so the mapping is man-page grounded but not host-demonstrated.

evidence.quote: Capabilities listed will be included in the bounding set, all others are removed.
this option also affects the respective capabilities in the effective, permitted and inheritable capability sets
This does not affect commands prefixed with "+".
Bypass file read, write, and execute permission checks.
This is the set of capabilities used by the kernel to perform permission checks for the thread.
The capability bounding set is a mechanism that can be used to limit the capabilities that are gained during execve(2).
for the root user, the check uses the set of permitted capabilities rather than the set of effective capabilities
access() does not answer the "can I read/write/execute this file?" question

branches.interpretation: User=root does not imply DAC bypass. A CapabilityBoundingSet= that omits CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE restricts the executed process's bounding set and, per S028, also affects the effective, permitted and inheritable sets; the DAC bypass (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, S027) is therefore not granted by the configured bounding set, and root is treated as DAC-bound under that configuration. For the EACCES class this branch is a conjunct of B1, not an alternative cause: it explains why a write-protected parent would not be bypassed. This is a configured restriction, not a measurement of the live process's CapEff/CapPrm: the kernel's actual permission checks use the effective set (S027 § Thread capability sets > Effective), which was unobserved, while S034/S038 describe a permission-check proxy, not an actual create.

commands: systemctl show -p User -p Group -p CapabilityBoundingSet -p AmbientCapabilities -p NoNewPrivileges <unit>
grep -E '^(CapPrm|CapEff|CapBnd):' /proc/<live-issuer-pid>/status (only when a live issuer PID is confirmed; never reuse a stale ExecMainPID)
discriminator.expected_signal: configured bounding set omits cap_dac_override and AmbientCapabilities is empty; when measurable, the live CapEff lacks bit 1 (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE). Bounding-set text alone is not a CapEff measurement.

branches.evidence_kind: configured unit text + optional read-only /proc caps; live effective sets unobserved in this round
branches.limit: Capability text is a process restriction, not a filesystem permission test (S028 registry note). With the unit inactive, systemctl show is configured text; the reported ExecMainPID was 1386 while `ps -p 1386` exited 1 (no such process), so it is a stale value and must never be used as a live PID. A live process's CapEff/CapPrm can only come from that process's /proc status; bounding-set text alone does not establish them, and the failing issuer may be a child, not ExecMainPID. access(2)/faccessat is a permission proxy, not an actual-operation authorization (S034/S038), and whether a probe uses access(2) or faccessat(AT_EACCESS) must be established per binary. The property text is also conditional: a systemd command prefixed with "+" is not affected by CapabilityBoundingSet= (S028), and the unit's ExecStart prefixes were not inspected here.

evidence.quote: path already exists (not necessarily as a directory). This includes the case where path is a symbolic link, dangling or not.

branches.interpretation: For ordinary mkdir/mkdirat, a target path that already exists as directory, file, subvolume mountpoint or dangling symlink yields EEXIST — a different errno and a different repair than EACCES. Presence is a B4-family indicator for that operation, not a universal target-present cause for other create mechanisms. In the snapshot context the collision class would be a pre-existing /.snapshots entry or mountpoint.

discriminator.expected_signal: stat succeeds for any file type (B4-family indicator for an ordinary mkdir), or stat reports no current entry with No such file or directory (ENOENT) text; findmnt can only report not-a-mountpoint, never absence

branches.evidence_kind: current target-path existence; historical failure-time state unobserved
branches.limit: The measured order (existing target under a 0555 parent -> EEXIST, new target -> EACCES) is for ordinary mkdir on this kernel (parent smoke, .ufo/waves/round-12/error-order-smoke.json). It is a diagnostic collection order for that operation, not a general syscall errno-priority rule, and it must not be extrapolated to the Btrfs subvolume ioctl used by the snapshot tool; an observed errno:13 therefore does not establish that the target was absent for that ioctl. The current absence of /.snapshots is a dated 2026-10-20 `stat` ENOENT observation, not a `findmnt` result, and does not reconstruct the target's state during the 2026-10-16..19 logged incidents.

decision_procedure: 0. Record the observed errno/API family first (13 EACCES, 17 EEXIST, 30 EROFS, 1 EPERM, other/unknown). The steps below collect indicators; they are not a universal syscall errno-priority proof.

1. For ordinary mkdir/mkdirat only, stat the target path (any type): present -> B4-family indicator; absent -> no current collision indicator. This is current-state evidence, not a failure-time proof, and does not transfer to the Btrfs subvolume ioctl.

2. Read the target mount's VFS/FS options (findmnt) and the unit's ProtectSystem/ReadOnlyPaths/ReadWritePaths: a read-only superblock, ProtectSystem=strict, or a ReadOnlyPaths= entry covering the target -> B2-family indicator (EROFS). ProtectSystem=full covers /usr,/boot,/efi,/etc, not /.

3. Read the parent mode/ACL and each path-prefix directory's search bit: write denied on the parent, or search denied on a path-prefix directory -> B1-family indicator (EACCES for ordinary mkdir when no bypass capability is effective).

4. Read the unit's User/CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities/NoNewPrivileges. A configured bounding set that omits cap_dac_override (non-root, or root bounded to e.g. cap_sys_admin) -> B3-family indicator. When a live issuer PID is confirmed, read CapEff/CapPrm from /proc; never infer them from the bounding set or a stale ExecMainPID.

5. Interpret the indicator set against the observed errno: B1 + B3 with a rw mount is consistent with an observed 13 for an ordinary mkdir; B2 is consistent with 30; B4 is consistent with 17. Do not convert a current-state indicator into proof of the historical failure.
6. No B1-B4 indicator fits the observed errno -> report UNCLASSIFIED; retain the residual (e.g. LSM/confinement, unit-private namespace, unknown operation ordering) and do not name a cause.
